title: The Red-Headed League
summary: A man with bright red hair gets a strange, easy job, and Sherlock Holmes wants to know why.

source.work: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, "The Red-Headed League"
source.author: Arthur Conan Doyle

chapters.title: A Strange Advertisement
sentences: One autumn morning, Dr Watson visited his friend Sherlock Holmes in Baker Street.
Holmes was talking to a large, older man with bright red hair.
The visitor's name was Jabez Wilson, and he owned a small shop in London.
"Please tell my friend your story from the beginning," Holmes said.
Mr Wilson took an old newspaper out of his pocket.
His young assistant had shown him an advertisement in it a few weeks earlier.
It said that a group called the Red-Headed League needed a new member.
The member would earn good money for very simple work.
The only condition was that the man had to have red hair.
Hundreds of red-haired men came to the office, but Mr Wilson got the job.
Every day, from ten until two, he copied pages from an encyclopedia.
He was not allowed to leave the office during those hours.
This went on for eight weeks, and the pay was always on time.
Then one morning he found a short note on the locked door.
It said that the Red-Headed League no longer existed.
Holmes smiled, because he thought this was a very interesting problem.

quiz.q: What did Mr Wilson have to do in his new job?
quiz.explain: From ten until two every day, he copied pages from an encyclopedia.

quiz.q: Why did Mr Wilson get the job?
options: He was a friend of Holmes.
He was the youngest man there.
quiz.explain: The only condition in the advertisement was red hair.

options: Mr Wilson left because he was bored.
He found a note saying the League no longer existed.
quiz.explain: One morning there was a note on the locked door: the League no longer existed.
